newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries up at midday before 10-year auction.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries up at midday before 10-year auction.

text.p: U.S. government securities prices were slightly higher at midday on Wednesday an hour before the Treasury's 10-year note auction.
The Treasury will sell $12.0 billion in 10-year notes this afternoon in the second leg of its three-part quarterly refunding operation.
The bidding deadline for the notes is 1300 EDT/1700 GMT.
The Treasury sold $16.0 billion in three-year notes on Tuesday and is scheduled to sell $10.0 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday.
At midday, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 6/32 to 101-30/32, yielding 6.48 percent, having erased modest early losses.
A central bank buyer of 10-year cash bonds and the purchase of 6,000 September bond contracts by a dealer were said to have aided the market.
Analysts said demand for the imminent 10-year bonds could come from mortgage-backed securities investors who need to lengthen the duration of their investment portfolios.
John Williams, managing director and chief global markets economist at Bankers Trust, said he expected the Treasury's 10-year note auction to go smoothly.

"We got a little bit of a price concession starting last Friday with the scare from the NAPM (National Association of Purchasing Management) index," said Williams. "But this week people are looking at that more as a potentially aberrant one-month number and they don't see a bad inflation number coming up real soon so they figure the 'don't worry, be happy' scenario can continue for a while."
